newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN says Zaire suspends aid work in eastern region.
newsitem.headline: UN says Zaire suspends aid work in eastern region.

text.p: Local authorities in eastern Zaire asked all international relief agencies on Friday to suspend aid activities in the Lubutu area near camps sheltering some 160,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees, the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR said.

"We've just heard about this...No reasons were given. It's not clear whether it's linked to the military or security situation there," spokeswoman Pamela O'Toole told a briefing. UNHCR was having urgent talks with local authorities.

"We're entering urgent discussions with local authorities in the area to see what it all means and what can be done about it," O'Toole said. "The situation is precarious. The refugees are in desperate need. If there are any kind of restrictions, it could cause tremendous problems."
There was no word on the suspension from Zaire's capital Kinshasa. Zaire's army launched an offensive against Tutsi-led rebels in the east on January 20.

O'Toole said the region had food waiting to be distributed but there could be problems if supplies were not increased within a week. She said aid agency vehicles and even small planes were being confiscated by the Zairean military in the region, further hampering relief efforts for refugees.

The Lubutu area, 240 km (150 miles) southeast of eastern Zaire's regional hub Kisangani, shelters around 160,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees who trekked deeper west into Zaire after Tutsi rebels overran their camps in October rather than joining some 600,000 who returned home to Rwanda.
